story.head: Round two in Nashville
paras: The Predators won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-2 in Nashville on Oct 17. The Preds have won three straight, while the Blues (7-7-2) lost 5-4 in overtime to New Jersey on Thursday. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Blues sixth (tied for 21st in the NHL) and the Predators fifth (tied for 14th).

The Blues have played better than their record (.500) says: their chances are worth about .561. The Predators’ record (.594) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.525), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games.

The Blues (lowest) and the Predators (3rd lowest) both keep things calm after the whistle. The Blues ice the puck less than almost anyone (3rd). They also have struggled on the power play (31st), so their struggling power play gets a tough test from the Predators’ penalty killers. As for the Predators, they get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd) and give up a lot of shots (31st).

Mason McTavish (7 G / 5 A / 12 P in 16 GP) leads the Blues in scoring, and Jimmy Snuggerud (8 G / 3 A / 11 P in 16 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Predators, Filip Forsberg (5 G / 14 A / 19 P in 16 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games and twelve goals in twelve games against St. Louis since 2023-24. Steven Stamkos (9 G / 8 A / 17 P in 16 GP) has a team-high nine goals.

Joel Hofer (6-4-1 / .918 SV% in 11 GS) has been outstanding for St. Louis and is expected to start. Juuse Saros (4-3-4 / .908 SV% in 11 GS) is expected to go for Nashville. Hofer has a .866 save percentage in seven starts against the Predators, well under his usual .912. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Andrew Brunette likes to send Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Holloway, Thomas and Snuggerud.
